note: Predictions are not evidence. Each prediction must eventually be linked to models, pilots, or rejected. Epistemic classes are not interchangeable with empirical claims.

predictions.text: Isolated corporate tax increases alone would likely produce modest effects and significant avoidance/adaptation.
Years 1–3 of system implementation would be dominated by structural work with limited wealth-gap movement.
If labor tax relief and ownership expansion occur together, median household wealth could eventually rise faster than GDP.
Illustrative household cash-flow gains of roughly $4,000–$8,000/year from labor-tax relief are design-dependent examples, not scored forecasts.
Broader local ownership and retained investment could improve community stability after employer exits.
Multiple ownership channels can compound household wealth in ways wages alone typically do not.
Successful long-horizon implementation would be remembered less as a tax reform and more as a shift toward an ownership-based middle class.
The largest poverty effect, if any, would likely be reduced chronic/intergenerational poverty through asset ownership rather than immediate poverty elimination.

A sufficiently broad Constitutional Capitalism reform package may produce larger long-run distributional effects than an isolated corporate-tax increase; this is an untested comparative prediction requiring defined policy specifications, distributional modeling, sensitivity analysis, and ultimately empirical evaluation.
predictions.note: Prediction — not empirical proof. Activated by CC-DEC-103 retirement of CC-CLAIM-009.
